task_1.title: Add DataTree.prune() method to remove empty nodes from tree
task_1.description: After filtering operations such as sel(), isel(), or where() on a DataTree, some nodes may become empty when their coordinate ranges do not overlap with the selection criteria. These leftover empty nodes clutter the tree structure and can confuse downstream processing. A new prune() method is added to DataTree that removes empty nodes while preserving intermediate nodes required to maintain the tree hierarchy for non-empty descendants. The method also provides an option to treat variables with zero-sized dimensions as empty.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that DataTree provides a prune() method that removes empty nodes from the tree after filtering or selection operations. When a DataTree undergoes operations like sel() or isel(), nodes whose coordinate ranges fall outside the selection criteria end up empty (no data variables, or all data variables with zero-sized dimensions). These empty nodes should be removable via a dedicated prune() call, returning a clean tree containing only nodes with actual data while keeping intermediate ancestor nodes necessary to maintain the path to non-empty descendants.

expectation.grounded: DataTree.prune(drop_size_zero_vars: bool = False) returns a new DataTree. By default, a node is considered non-empty if it has at least one data variable (len(node.data_vars) > 0). When drop_size_zero_vars=True, a node is considered non-empty only if it has at least one data variable whose size is greater than zero. Intermediate nodes that are themselves empty but are ancestors of non-empty nodes are preserved to maintain tree path integrity. The method delegates to DataTree.filter() with the appropriate predicate. The original tree is not mutated.
expectation.conceptual: Calling prune() on a DataTree returns a new tree with empty nodes removed. By default, nodes that have no data variables are pruned. An optional flag allows also pruning nodes where all data variables have zero-sized dimensions. Ancestor nodes that are empty themselves but required to reach non-empty descendants are retained. The operation is non-mutating.

constraints.grounded: prune() must return a new DataTree instance and must not modify the original tree. The default behavior (drop_size_zero_vars=False) must retain nodes that have data variables even if those variables have zero-sized dimensions. When drop_size_zero_vars=True, nodes are pruned only when all of their data variables have size zero. Coordinate information in retained nodes must be preserved. The root node must always be present in the returned tree. The method must be consistent with DataTree.filter() semantics for intermediate node preservation.
constraints.conceptual: The pruning operation must be non-destructive to the source tree. The default mode must only remove nodes with no data variables at all, while the stricter mode additionally removes nodes whose variables are all zero-sized. Tree structural integrity must be maintained: ancestor nodes needed to connect the root to non-empty descendants must be kept. Coordinate metadata on retained nodes must not be altered.

behavior: DataTree.prune() with default arguments removes nodes that have zero data variables and returns a new DataTree
DataTree.prune(drop_size_zero_vars=True) additionally removes nodes where all data variables have size zero
Intermediate (ancestor) nodes that are empty but have non-empty descendants are preserved to maintain tree path structure
The root node is always present in the returned tree
The original DataTree is not modified; a new tree is returned
Nodes with at least one data variable with size > 0 are always retained regardless of the drop_size_zero_vars flag
Coordinate information on retained nodes is preserved unchanged
acceptance_criteria: When a DataTree has nodes with no data variables, calling prune() returns a new tree without those empty nodes
When a DataTree has nodes with zero-sized data variables, calling prune() with default arguments retains those nodes
When calling prune(drop_size_zero_vars=True), nodes whose data variables all have size zero are removed from the returned tree
When an intermediate node is empty but has a non-empty descendant, the intermediate node is retained in the pruned tree to preserve the path hierarchy
When prune() is called, the original DataTree remains unchanged with all its original nodes intact

Given a DataTree created after a sel() operation that leaves some nodes empty (zero-length dimensions), calling prune(drop_size_zero_vars=True) returns a tree containing only the nodes whose coordinate ranges overlapped with the selection criteria
When all child nodes of a subtree are empty, pruning removes the entire subtree including the parent node (unless the parent itself has data)

task_4.title: Add errors parameter to open_mfdataset for handling invalid files
task_4.description: When opening multiple files via open_mfdataset, encountering an invalid file (e.g., zero-byte, corrupt, or unreadable) previously raised an opaque exception with no indication of which file caused the failure. A new 'errors' parameter is introduced to open_mfdataset that allows users to control how invalid files are handled: raise an exception (default, preserving backward compatibility), emit a warning identifying the problematic file, or silently ignore invalid files. When invalid files are skipped, the internal path structure and concatenation ordering are correctly recalculated so the remaining valid datasets combine as expected.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that open_mfdataset provides a mechanism to gracefully handle invalid files among a batch of inputs. When one or more files in a multi-file open operation are invalid (corrupt, zero-byte, or unreadable), the user should be able to choose whether to raise an exception, receive a warning identifying each problematic file, or silently skip invalid files. The default behavior must remain raising an exception to preserve backward compatibility.

expectation.grounded: open_mfdataset accepts a new 'errors' parameter of type ErrorOptionsWithWarn with allowed values 'raise', 'warn', and 'ignore', defaulting to 'raise'. When errors='raise', any exception from opening an individual file propagates immediately. When errors='warn', a user-level warning is emitted via emit_user_level_warning for each file that fails to open, and that file is excluded from the resulting dataset. When errors='ignore', files that fail to open are silently excluded. After excluding invalid paths, the internal path structure is pruned via _remove_path, and when combine='nested', concatenation order IDs are recalculated via _infer_concat_order_from_positions. A ValueError is raised if the errors parameter receives a value outside the three allowed options.
expectation.conceptual: open_mfdataset gains an errors parameter that controls behavior when individual files fail to open. In raise mode, the original exception propagates. In warn mode, a warning is emitted for each invalid file identifying the file path and the cause, and processing continues with the remaining valid files. In ignore mode, invalid files are silently skipped. The returned dataset is produced only from successfully opened files, with correct combine ordering maintained regardless of how many files were skipped.

constraints.grounded: The default value of the errors parameter must be 'raise', ensuring that existing callers experience no change in behavior. When errors is set to an unsupported value, a ValueError must be raised with a message indicating the allowed options. When invalid files are removed and combine='nested' is used, the concatenation IDs must be re-derived from the pruned path structure. The _remove_path helper must handle arbitrarily nested path sequences and must not introduce empty sub-lists into the result.
constraints.conceptual: Backward compatibility must be preserved: callers that do not pass the new parameter must see identical behavior to previous versions. Invalid parameter values must be rejected with a clear error. When files are skipped, the dataset combination logic must correctly account for the reduced set of inputs regardless of the combine strategy used.

behavior: open_mfdataset accepts a new keyword argument 'errors' with allowed values 'raise', 'warn', and 'ignore', defaulting to 'raise'.
When errors='raise' and a file fails to open, the original exception is re-raised immediately, preserving the prior default behavior.
When errors='warn' and a file fails to open, a user-level warning is emitted that includes the file path and the exception message, and the file is excluded from further processing.
When errors='ignore' and a file fails to open, the file is silently excluded from further processing with no warning or error.
After all files are attempted, any invalid paths are pruned from the nested path structure so that downstream combine logic operates only on valid entries.
When combine='nested' and invalid files were removed, the concatenation order IDs are recalculated from the pruned path positions.
Passing an unsupported value for errors raises a ValueError indicating the allowed options.
The path removal logic correctly handles arbitrarily nested path sequences and omits empty sub-lists from the result.
acceptance_criteria: When open_mfdataset is called with a mix of valid and invalid files and errors='raise', it should raise an exception on the first invalid file encountered.

When open_mfdataset is called with a mix of valid and invalid files and errors='warn', it should emit a warning for each invalid file that includes the file path and error cause, and return a dataset composed only from the valid files.
When open_mfdataset is called with a mix of valid and invalid files and errors='ignore', it should silently skip invalid files and return a dataset composed only from the valid files.
When open_mfdataset is called without the errors parameter, it should behave identically to errors='raise', preserving backward compatibility.
When open_mfdataset is called with errors set to an unsupported value (e.g., 'skip'), it should raise a ValueError.
When combine='nested' and some files are invalid with errors='warn' or errors='ignore', the resulting dataset should have correctly ordered concatenation dimensions reflecting only the valid files.
When all files in the input are invalid and errors='warn' or errors='ignore', open_mfdataset should handle the empty dataset list gracefully.
When paths contain nested lists and some inner paths are invalid, the pruned path structure should not contain empty sub-lists.

task_5.title: Avoid redefining inherited dimensions in NetCDF group writes
task_5.description: When writing a DataTree to NetCDF, Xarray previously redefined dimensions in every subgroup even when a parent group already defined the same dimension with the same size. This produced non-conformant NetCDF files that duplicated dimension definitions across groups. The fix ensures child groups inherit dimensions from ancestor groups per CF Conventions for group scope, only creating a local dimension when its size differs from the nearest ancestor's definition. This changes the on-disk structure of NetCDF files produced by Xarray and may require adjustments in downstream code that consumes those files.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when a DataTree is written to NetCDF, dimensions already defined in a parent group with the same size are not redundantly redefined in child groups. Previously, every subgroup would declare its own copy of dimensions like 'x' and 'y' even though they were already present (with matching sizes) in the root or an ancestor group. The resulting files violated CF Conventions for group scope, which specify that dimensions are inherited from parent groups.

expectation.grounded: AbstractWritableDataStore.set_dimensions must consult the new get_parent_dimensions method (backed by collect_ancestor_dimensions) before calling set_dimension. A dimension should only be created in a child group when its required size differs from the size returned by get_parent_dimensions for that dimension name. Both NetCDF4DataStore and H5NetCDFStore must implement get_parent_dimensions to walk ancestor groups and return their dimension name-to-size mapping. The base AbstractDataStore.get_parent_dimensions must return an empty dict so non-hierarchical backends are unaffected.
expectation.conceptual: When writing hierarchical datasets to NetCDF, child groups must not redefine dimensions that already exist with the same size in any ancestor group. Dimensions should only be explicitly created in a child group when the child requires a different size than what would be inherited. This applies to all NetCDF-backed storage engines that support grouped writes.

constraints.grounded: If a child group requires a dimension with a size that differs from the ancestor's definition of the same dimension name, that dimension must still be created locally in the child group. Existing error behavior when attempting to update the size of an already-existing local dimension must be preserved. Backends that do not support hierarchical groups (get_parent_dimensions returns empty dict) must remain unaffected. Unlimited dimensions must continue to be handled correctly in the dimension ordering and creation logic.
constraints.conceptual: Dimension inheritance must only suppress creation when sizes match; mismatched sizes must still produce a local dimension. Non-hierarchical write paths must not change behavior. The fix must not alter how unlimited dimensions are declared or ordered. Error handling for conflicting dimension sizes within the same group must be preserved.

behavior: When writing a DataTree to NetCDF, dimensions defined in a parent group are now inherited by child groups instead of being redefined, conforming to CF Conventions for group scope.
The writable data store now queries ancestor groups for their dimension definitions before deciding whether to create a new dimension in the current group.
A dimension is only created in a child group if it does not exist locally AND its required size differs from the nearest ancestor's definition of that dimension.
Both the netCDF4 and h5netcdf backends now expose parent dimension information via get_parent_dimensions.
NetCDF files produced by DataTree.to_netcdf will have a different on-disk structure: child groups will no longer contain redundant dimension declarations for dimensions inherited from ancestors.
acceptance_criteria: When a DataTree with shared dimensions (e.g., 'x', 'y' defined in root and used in child groups) is written to NetCDF, the resulting file's child groups must not contain dimension definitions for dimensions already defined with the same size in a parent group.
When inspecting the written NetCDF file (e.g., via netCDF4.Dataset or ncdump), child groups that only use inherited dimensions should show no local dimension declarations.
When a child group requires a dimension with a different size than the parent's definition, that dimension must be created locally in the child group.
When writing a flat (non-grouped) Dataset to NetCDF, behavior must be identical to the previous version with no regressions.

When writing a DataTree where the root defines dimensions 'y(2)' and 'x(2)', and a child group '/data' has a variable using those same dimensions with the same sizes, the child group in the output file must inherit 'y' and 'x' from root rather than redefining them.
When unlimited dimensions are used in grouped writes, they must continue to be declared and ordered correctly regardless of the inheritance optimization.

task_2.title: Add asynchronous load_async() methods to Dataset, DataArray, and Variable
task_2.description: Introduces new asynchronous loading methods (load_async) on Dataset, DataArray, and Variable that allow non-blocking, concurrent data loading from high-latency IO backends such as Zarr on remote object storage. Previously, all load() calls were synchronous, forcing users to rely on dask for any concurrency. With zarr v3 exposing async array access, xarray now plumbs async retrieval through its entire indexing chain and exposes it as a user-facing async API. Users are responsible for managing concurrency (e.g., via asyncio.gather); xarray does not internally limit concurrency. Backends that do not support async loading will raise NotImplementedError.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Dataset, DataArray, and Variable each expose a load_async() coroutine method that asynchronously loads lazily-opened data into memory from IO backends that support async access. The method must behave like the existing load() (modifying and returning the original object) but operate as an awaitable coroutine, enabling users to concurrently load multiple xarray objects without requiring dask. Backends that do not support asynchronous loading must raise NotImplementedError when load_async is invoked.

expectation.grounded: Variable.load_async(), DataArray.load_async(), and Dataset.load_async() are public async methods returning Self. Variable.load_async() delegates to async_to_duck_array() which calls async_get_duck_array() on the underlying indexing wrapper. DataArray.load_async() converts to a temporary Dataset and awaits its load_async(). Dataset.load_async() handles chunked (dask) arrays synchronously via chunkmanager.compute(), then concurrently awaits load_async() on all remaining variables using asyncio.gather(). IndexVariable.load_async() returns self immediately since index data is already in memory. The async path flows through async_get_duck_array() on ExplicitlyIndexedNDArrayMixin subclasses, async_getitem() on BackendArray subclasses, and async_explicit_indexing_adapter(). The base BackendArray.async_getitem() raises NotImplementedError. ZarrArrayWrapper implements async_getitem() by dispatching to _async_getitem, _async_oindex, or _async_vindex based on indexer type (BasicIndexer, OuterIndexer, VectorizedIndexer). Basic async zarr indexing requires zarr v3.0.0+; orthogonal and vectorized async indexing require zarr v3.1.2+ (presence of oindex on zarr.AsyncArray). A new IndexingAdapter marker class is introduced as the base for in-memory array adapters (NumpyIndexingAdapter, ArrayApiIndexingAdapter, DaskIndexingAdapter, PandasIndexingAdapter, CoordinateTransformIndexingAdapter), providing a default async_get_duck_array() that falls back to the synchronous get_duck_array(). ExplicitlyIndexedNDArrayMixin.get_duck_array() and async_get_duck_array() now both raise NotImplementedError by default. CopyOnWriteArray, MemoryCachedArray, LazilyIndexedArray, LazilyVectorizedIndexedArray, and _ElementwiseFunctionArray all implement async_get_duck_array() to propagate async loading through the wrapping chain.
expectation.conceptual: Dataset, DataArray, and Variable each gain a load_async() coroutine that asynchronously loads lazily-referenced data into memory and returns the modified object. When awaited, the method resolves all lazy backend-sourced data without blocking the event loop, enabling concurrent loading of multiple objects via standard asyncio patterns like asyncio.gather(). Chunked (dask-backed) data within a Dataset is still computed synchronously; only non-chunked lazy variables are loaded asynchronously. If the underlying storage backend does not support async loading, a NotImplementedError is raised. IndexVariable.load_async() is a no-op since its data is always in memory. Xarray does not impose any concurrency limits; users must manage concurrency themselves.

constraints.grounded: The existing synchronous load() and compute() methods on Variable, DataArray, and Dataset must continue to work identically. The refactoring of get_duck_array() in LazilyIndexedArray and LazilyVectorizedIndexedArray (switching from ExplicitlyIndexedNDArrayMixin isinstance checks to BackendArray isinstance checks) must not change synchronous loading behavior. The re-parenting of NumpyIndexingAdapter, ArrayApiIndexingAdapter, DaskIndexingAdapter, PandasIndexingAdapter, and CoordinateTransformIndexingAdapter from ExplicitlyIndexedNDArrayMixin to IndexingAdapter must not alter their synchronous indexing behavior. BackendArray subclasses that do not override async_getitem() must raise NotImplementedError when async loading is attempted. The MemoryCachedArray must cache the result of async_get_duck_array() in self.array, matching the caching semantics of the synchronous path. load_async() must return Self (the same object, mutated in-place), consistent with load().
constraints.conceptual: All existing synchronous loading and computation workflows must remain unaffected. The async loading feature must only activate when explicitly called by the user via load_async(); it must not change default loading behavior. Backend implementations that lack async support must fail clearly with NotImplementedError rather than silently degrading. The in-memory caching behavior of intermediate indexing wrappers must be preserved in the async path. The async API must not introduce any internal concurrency limiting or throttling.

behavior: Calling await Variable.load_async() on a variable backed by an async-capable backend loads its data into memory asynchronously and stores the result in the variable's _data attribute
Calling await DataArray.load_async() delegates to Dataset.load_async() via a temporary dataset conversion, then updates the DataArray's variable and coordinates in-place
Calling await Dataset.load_async() first computes any chunked (dask) arrays synchronously, then concurrently awaits load_async() on all remaining non-chunked variables using asyncio.gather()
IndexVariable.load_async() returns self immediately without any async operation since index data is always in memory
When a BackendArray subclass does not implement async_getitem(), calling load_async() raises NotImplementedError
ZarrArrayWrapper dispatches async loading through basic, outer, or vectorized async indexing methods depending on the indexer type
ZarrArrayWrapper raises NotImplementedError for basic async indexing if zarr version is below v3.0.0
ZarrArrayWrapper raises NotImplementedError for orthogonal or vectorized async indexing if zarr.AsyncArray lacks oindex support (zarr below v3.1.2)
MemoryCachedArray.async_get_duck_array() caches the loaded result in self.array, matching synchronous caching behavior
CopyOnWriteArray.async_get_duck_array() delegates to the wrapped array's async_get_duck_array()
_ElementwiseFunctionArray.async_get_duck_array() applies its element-wise function to the result of the inner array's async_get_duck_array()
In-memory indexing adapters (NumpyIndexingAdapter, DaskIndexingAdapter, etc.) inherit from IndexingAdapter and their async_get_duck_array() falls back to synchronous get_duck_array()
acceptance_criteria: When a Variable is lazily backed by a zarr v3 store, calling await variable.load_async() should load the data into memory and return the same Variable object with in-memory data
When a DataArray is lazily backed by a zarr v3 store, calling await dataarray.load_async() should load all data and coordinates into memory and return the same DataArray object
When a Dataset with multiple lazy variables is backed by zarr v3, calling await dataset.load_async() should load all variables concurrently into memory and return the same Dataset
When a Dataset contains both chunked (dask) and non-chunked lazy variables, load_async() should compute dask arrays synchronously and load non-chunked variables asynchronously
When multiple DataArrays are loaded concurrently via asyncio.gather([da.load_async() for da in dataarrays]), all should load in parallel rather than sequentially
When load_async() is called on a Variable backed by a backend that does not implement async_getitem(), a NotImplementedError should be raised
When async basic indexing is attempted with zarr < v3.0.0, a NotImplementedError should be raised indicating the version requirement
When async orthogonal or vectorized indexing is attempted with zarr lacking AsyncArray.oindex (< v3.1.2), a NotImplementedError should be raised indicating the version requirement
Calling IndexVariable.load_async() should return self immediately without performing any async I/O
The existing synchronous load() method on Variable, DataArray, and Dataset should continue to work unchanged after this update
The existing compute() method on Variable, DataArray, and Dataset should continue to work unchanged
After await variable.load_async(), the variable's data should be an in-memory array, not a lazy reference
MemoryCachedArray should cache the result after async_get_duck_array() is called, so subsequent access does not re-fetch from the backend

task_3.title: Support DataTree.to_netcdf() writing to file-like objects or returning in-memory bytes
task_3.description: DataTree.to_netcdf() previously required a filesystem path and could not write to file-like objects or return in-memory data. This update extends DataTree.to_netcdf() to accept file-like objects (e.g. io.BytesIO) and to return a memoryview when called without a filepath, matching the existing behavior of Dataset.to_netcdf(). Additionally, Dataset.to_netcdf() and DataArray.to_netcdf() now support the h5netcdf engine for in-memory and file-like writes (previously only scipy was allowed), and their return type when path is None may now be memoryview instead of bytes depending on the engine. The scipy engine emits a FutureWarning that its bytes return will switch to memoryview in a future version. Open functions (open_dataset, open_dataarray, open_datatree, open_groups) now also accept bytes and memoryview as input types.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that DataTree.to_netcdf() can write to a file-like object (e.g. io.BytesIO) or return in-memory data as a memoryview when called without a filepath argument. Ensure that Dataset.to_netcdf() and DataArray.to_netcdf() support the h5netcdf engine when writing to file-like objects or returning in-memory data, and that their return type reflects either bytes or memoryview depending on engine. Ensure that open_dataset, open_dataarray, open_datatree, and open_groups accept bytes and memoryview objects as input.

expectation.grounded: DataTree.to_netcdf() should accept filepath as None, str, PathLike, or io.IOBase. When filepath is None, it should return a memoryview containing valid netCDF4 data. When filepath is a file-like object supporting read, write, and seek, the data should be written to that object and None returned. DataTree.to_netcdf() should default to engine='h5netcdf' when no engine is specified. Dataset.to_netcdf() and DataArray.to_netcdf() with path=None should return bytes when using engine='scipy' and memoryview when using engine='h5netcdf'. The to_netcdf() function should accept engine='h5netcdf' in addition to engine='scipy' for in-memory and file-like writes, raising ValueError for any other engine. When the scipy engine is used for an in-memory write (path=None), a FutureWarning should be emitted indicating the return type will change from bytes to memoryview. open_dataset, open_dataarray, open_datatree, and open_groups should accept bytes and memoryview objects, wrapping them in BytesIO internally for backend consumption. The guess_engine function and all backend guess_can_open methods should handle bytes and memoryview inputs.
expectation.conceptual: DataTree.to_netcdf() should support the same in-memory and file-like output patterns as Dataset.to_netcdf(). Calling it without a filepath should return the serialized netCDF content in memory. Calling it with a seekable file-like object should write directly to that object. All netCDF open functions should accept raw bytes or memoryview objects representing file contents in addition to paths and file-like objects. The h5netcdf engine should be usable for in-memory writes across Dataset, DataArray, and DataTree. The scipy engine should warn about an upcoming change in its in-memory return type.

constraints.grounded: DataTree.to_netcdf() must only support NETCDF4 format and only the netcdf4 and h5netcdf engines, raising ValueError otherwise. The to_netcdf() function must raise ValueError if an engine other than None, 'scipy', or 'h5netcdf' is specified for in-memory or file-like writes. compute=False must raise NotImplementedError for in-memory writes. The FutureWarning for scipy engine in-memory writes must be emitted at user level. The h5netcdf backend must not attempt to read a magic number from file-like objects opened in write mode. The DummyFileManager close behavior for file-like objects passed to scipy must call flush instead of close to avoid prematurely closing the file object. Existing Dataset.to_netcdf() behavior for file-path writes must remain unchanged. The group parameter on DataTree.to_netcdf() must still raise NotImplementedError.
constraints.conceptual: Existing write-to-path behavior for Dataset, DataArray, and DataTree must not regress. File-like objects that do not support seek may not work due to underlying HDF5 library limitations. The in-memory write feature for DataTree must use an engine that supports groups (not scipy). The deprecation path for the scipy engine's bytes return type must be communicated via a warning before any breaking change.

behavior: DataTree.to_netcdf() with filepath=None returns a memoryview of valid netCDF4 content using the h5netcdf engine by default
DataTree.to_netcdf() with a file-like object (io.IOBase) writes netCDF4 data to that object and returns None
DataTree.to_netcdf() has proper overloaded signatures: filepath=None returns memoryview, filepath as path/file-like returns None
Dataset.to_netcdf() and DataArray.to_netcdf() with path=None now accept engine='h5netcdf' and return memoryview
Dataset.to_netcdf() and DataArray.to_netcdf() with path=None and engine='scipy' emit a FutureWarning about the return type changing from bytes to memoryview
Dataset.to_netcdf() and DataArray.to_netcdf() accept io.IOBase file-like objects as the path parameter
to_netcdf() raises ValueError when an unsupported engine is specified for in-memory or file-like writes (only None, 'scipy', 'h5netcdf' allowed)
open_dataset, open_dataarray, open_datatree, and open_groups accept bytes and memoryview as filename_or_obj, wrapping them in BytesIO for backend processing
H5NetCDFStore.open() skips the magic number validation check when opening a file-like object in write mode
H5NetCDFStore.open() uses h5netcdf.File directly (not CachingFileManager) for non-string file-like inputs
ScipyDataStore wraps file-like objects using flush instead of close to prevent scipy from prematurely closing passed-in file objects
The guess_engine function and all backend guess_can_open methods accept bytes and memoryview inputs via the unified T_PathFileOrDataStore type
acceptance_criteria: When DataTree.to_netcdf() is called with no filepath argument, it should return a memoryview that can be used to reconstruct the DataTree via open_datatree
When DataTree.to_netcdf(io.BytesIO()) is called with a BytesIO object, the BytesIO object should contain valid netCDF4 data and the method should return None
When DataTree.to_netcdf() is called with filepath=None and no engine specified, it should default to the h5netcdf engine
When Dataset.to_netcdf() is called with path=None and engine='h5netcdf', it should return a memoryview
When Dataset.to_netcdf() is called with path=None and engine='scipy' (or default), it should emit a FutureWarning and return bytes
When to_netcdf() is called with path=None and engine='netcdf4', it should raise a ValueError
When open_dataset is called with bytes or memoryview containing valid netCDF data, it should successfully open and return a Dataset
When open_datatree is called with bytes or memoryview containing valid netCDF4 data, it should successfully open and return a DataTree
When DataTree.to_netcdf() is called with an unsupported format, it should raise ValueError mentioning only NETCDF4 is supported
When DataTree.to_netcdf() is called with an unsupported engine, it should raise ValueError mentioning only netcdf4 and h5netcdf are supported
When a DataTree is round-tripped via to_netcdf() with no filepath and then open_datatree() on the returned memoryview, the data should be preserved

task_7.title: Fix Pydap Datatree backend flaky tests by using set comparison
task_7.description: The Pydap Datatree backend tests were flaky because they compared two lists whose elements matched but whose order could differ between runs. The fix changes the comparison to use unordered set equality instead of ordered list equality, eliminating the non-deterministic test failures.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the Pydap Datatree backend tests do not fail intermittently due to element ordering. The tests previously compared two ordered lists, but the underlying data source does not guarantee a stable element order, causing spurious test failures.

expectation.grounded: The Pydap Datatree backend test assertions should use unordered (set-based) comparison for collections returned by the Datatree backend where element order is not guaranteed. All existing test cases for the Pydap Datatree backend should pass deterministically regardless of the order in which elements are returned.
expectation.conceptual: Tests validating the Pydap Datatree backend should be resilient to non-deterministic element ordering. When comparing collections of returned elements, the tests should verify that the same elements are present without requiring a specific order.

constraints.grounded: The change must be limited to test assertions only; no runtime behavior of the Pydap Datatree backend or its public API should be altered. The test coverage must remain equivalent — all previously asserted elements must still be verified for presence and correctness.
constraints.conceptual: Only test comparison logic should change. The backend's runtime behavior, public API, and data correctness guarantees must remain unaffected. Test coverage must not regress.

behavior: Pydap Datatree backend tests previously compared results as ordered lists, causing intermittent failures when element order differed across runs.
After the fix, the same tests compare results as unordered sets, so equivalent collections in any order are treated as equal.
No change to runtime behavior — the Pydap Datatree backend itself is unmodified.
acceptance_criteria: When running the Pydap Datatree backend tests repeatedly, they should pass deterministically without order-dependent failures.
When the Pydap Datatree backend returns elements in any permutation, the tests should still pass as long as the same elements are present.
When a genuinely missing or extra element is returned by the backend, the tests should still detect and report the mismatch.
No runtime behavior of the xarray Pydap Datatree backend should be altered by this change.

task_8.title: Fix KeyError in convert_calendar when using a non-default dim argument
task_8.description: When calling xarray's convert_calendar with a dim argument other than the default 'time', a KeyError was raised because an internal selection step hardcoded the dimension name 'time' instead of using the caller-supplied dim parameter. This regression was introduced by a prior fix (PR #10268). The fix ensures the NaN-filtering selection step uses the actual dimension name provided by the user.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that convert_calendar does not raise a KeyError when the user supplies a dim argument that differs from the default value 'time'. The function must correctly use the caller-specified dimension name throughout its entire execution path, including the step that removes NaN entries corresponding to invalid dates in the target calendar.

expectation.grounded: When convert_calendar is called with a custom dim argument (e.g., dim='forecast_time'), the internal .sel() call that filters out NaN values for invalid target-calendar dates must select along the user-specified dimension rather than the hardcoded 'time'. The function should return a Dataset or DataArray with the converted calendar indexed by the custom dimension, with no KeyError raised.
expectation.conceptual: convert_calendar should work correctly regardless of which dimension name the user specifies for the time coordinate. Users who name their time dimension something other than 'time' should experience the same correct calendar-conversion behavior as those using the default dimension name.

constraints.grounded: The default behavior of convert_calendar when dim='time' (or when dim is not specified) must remain unchanged. The NaN-filtering selection must still correctly remove entries that correspond to dates that are invalid in the target calendar. No other convert_calendar code paths should be affected.
constraints.conceptual: Fixing the non-default dim path must not regress the default dim='time' path. Calendar conversion correctness—including proper removal of invalid dates—must be preserved for all dimension names.

behavior: Previously, calling convert_calendar with dim set to any value other than 'time' raised a KeyError because the NaN-removal step always selected on the literal dimension name 'time'.
After the fix, the NaN-removal selection uses the dimension name provided by the caller, so convert_calendar completes successfully for any valid dimension name.
When dim='time' (the default), behavior is unchanged; NaN entries for invalid target-calendar dates are still correctly removed.
acceptance_criteria: When convert_calendar is called with a non-default dim argument (e.g., dim='forecast_time'), it should complete without raising a KeyError.
When convert_calendar is called with a non-default dim argument, the returned object should have its calendar-converted coordinate indexed under the user-specified dimension name.
When convert_calendar is called with a non-default dim argument, dates that are invalid in the target calendar should still be removed (NaN filtering must work correctly on the custom dimension).
When convert_calendar is called with the default dim='time' (or without specifying dim), behavior should be identical to before the fix.

Given a Dataset with a time-like dimension named something other than 'time', when convert_calendar is invoked specifying that dimension, then the output should contain only valid dates in the target calendar with no KeyError.

task_9.title: Fix transpose of boolean and native-endianness arrays read from disk
task_9.description: Calling transpose() on boolean arrays loaded lazily from disk (e.g., via open_dataset) raised an AttributeError because the BoolTypeArray coding wrapper lacked a transpose method. The same gap existed in NativeEndiannessArray. This was a regression introduced in v2025.7.0. The fix adds transpose delegation to both wrapper classes and refactors the lazy indexing resolution hierarchy so that coding wrappers are required to implement get_duck_array explicitly rather than inheriting a fallback.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that calling .transpose() on a Dataset or DataArray containing boolean data loaded lazily from a NetCDF (or other backend) file no longer raises an AttributeError on the BoolTypeArray wrapper. The same must hold for arrays wrapped by NativeEndiannessArray. This was a regression from v2025.7.0 where transpose worked on lazily-loaded boolean data in prior versions.

expectation.grounded: BoolTypeArray and NativeEndiannessArray must each expose a transpose(order) method that delegates to their wrapped array's transpose, returning a new instance of the same wrapper type around the transposed inner array. LazilyIndexedArray.get_duck_array and LazilyVectorizedIndexedArray.get_duck_array must resolve coding wrappers (ExplicitlyIndexed subclasses) by calling get_duck_array on them after apply_indexer, while BackendArray instances are resolved via direct __getitem__. ExplicitlyIndexedNDArrayMixin.get_duck_array must raise NotImplementedError to force subclasses to provide their own implementation.
expectation.conceptual: Boolean and native-endianness coding wrappers must support the transpose operation so that lazily-loaded data from any backend can be transposed without first loading into memory. The lazy indexing layer must correctly propagate data-resolution calls through the wrapper chain regardless of whether the underlying array is a backend array or a coding adapter.

constraints.grounded: Transposing a lazily-loaded boolean DataArray must produce the same result as transposing the in-memory equivalent (loaded via .load()). The transpose on BoolTypeArray and NativeEndiannessArray must preserve the dtype-casting behavior of the wrapper (boolean casting and endianness conversion respectively). The refactored get_duck_array in LazilyIndexedArray and LazilyVectorizedIndexedArray must not change behavior for existing BackendArray or in-memory array paths.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must not alter the observable result of any previously working transpose or data-access operation. Coding wrappers must remain transparent to the user — transposition should yield identical data whether the array is loaded eagerly or accessed lazily.

behavior: BoolTypeArray.transpose(order) returns a new BoolTypeArray wrapping the transposed inner array, preserving boolean dtype decoding.
NativeEndiannessArray.transpose(order) returns a new NativeEndiannessArray wrapping the transposed inner array, preserving endianness conversion.
ExplicitlyIndexedNDArrayMixin.get_duck_array() now raises NotImplementedError instead of providing a default slice-based implementation.
A new IndexingAdapter subclass of ExplicitlyIndexedNDArrayMixin provides the former default get_duck_array implementation for indexing adapter classes.
LazilyIndexedArray.get_duck_array() distinguishes BackendArray (resolved via __getitem__) from other ExplicitlyIndexed arrays (resolved via apply_indexer then recursive get_duck_array).
LazilyVectorizedIndexedArray.get_duck_array() follows the same BackendArray vs ExplicitlyIndexed dispatch pattern.
acceptance_criteria: When a Dataset containing boolean variables is written to NetCDF and re-opened with open_dataset, calling .transpose() on the lazy dataset succeeds without raising AttributeError.
When a DataArray backed by a BoolTypeArray wrapper is transposed, the resulting array values are identical to transposing the eagerly-loaded (.load()) equivalent.
When a DataArray backed by a NativeEndiannessArray wrapper is transposed, the resulting array values and dtype are correct.
When get_duck_array is called on a LazilyIndexedArray wrapping a BackendArray, the backend's __getitem__ is used for resolution (not apply_indexer).
When get_duck_array is called on a LazilyIndexedArray wrapping a coding wrapper (e.g., BoolTypeArray), apply_indexer is used and the result is further resolved via the wrapper's own get_duck_array.
Subclasses of ExplicitlyIndexedNDArrayMixin that do not implement get_duck_array raise NotImplementedError when it is called.

task_6.title: Deprecation cycle for stricter combine/concat/merge/open_mfdataset default keyword arguments
task_6.description: Begins a deprecation cycle to change the default keyword arguments for concat(), merge(), combine_nested(), combine_by_coords(), and open_mfdataset() from permissive defaults (data_vars='all', coords='different', compat='no_conflicts', join='outer') to stricter, more performant defaults (data_vars=None, coords='minimal', compat='override', join='exact'). The old permissive defaults caused silent performance issues (slow reindex and unnecessary data reads), dimension size ballooning from floating-point index mismatches, and hard-to-understand concatenation behavior. A FutureWarning is emitted when old defaults would produce different behavior than the incoming new defaults, and a global option use_new_combine_kwarg_defaults allows users to opt in to new defaults immediately. The data_vars parameter now also accepts None, which dynamically selects 'all' when concatenating along a new dimension and 'minimal' when concatenating along an existing dimension.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the combine functions (concat, merge, combine_nested, combine_by_coords, open_mfdataset) begin a deprecation cycle for their default keyword arguments, transitioning from overly permissive defaults to stricter, more predictable, and more performant defaults. Ensure that a FutureWarning is emitted when the user has not explicitly set a keyword argument and the old default would produce different behavior than the new default. Ensure that a new global option (use_new_combine_kwarg_defaults) allows users to opt in to the new defaults immediately. Ensure that data_vars accepts None as a new semantic value meaning dimension-aware automatic selection. Ensure that internal callers of these functions pass explicit keyword arguments so they do not trigger deprecation warnings.

expectation.grounded: When calling concat(), merge(), combine_nested(), combine_by_coords(), or open_mfdataset() without explicitly setting data_vars, coords, compat, or join, a CombineKwargDefault sentinel is used instead of a hardcoded string default. If the option use_new_combine_kwarg_defaults is False (the default), the old values (data_vars='all', coords='different', compat='no_conflicts' or 'equals' for concat, join='outer') are used, but a FutureWarning is emitted whenever the output would differ under new defaults (data_vars=None, coords='minimal', compat='override', join='exact'). If use_new_combine_kwarg_defaults is True, the new default values are used immediately, and error messages from AlignmentError or MergeError are augmented with context about the default change. When data_vars is None (or the CombineKwargDefault resolves to None), it behaves as 'all' when concatenating along a new dimension and 'minimal' when concatenating along an existing dimension. Passing data_vars='minimal' together with coords='minimal' when concatenating over a new dimension raises ValueError. The set_options context manager accepts use_new_combine_kwarg_defaults as a boolean option.
expectation.conceptual: When users call combine functions without specifying keyword arguments for data_vars, coords, compat, or join, the library should warn (via FutureWarning) if the upcoming stricter defaults would produce different results than the current permissive defaults. Users should be able to opt in to the new defaults immediately via a global option. The new data_vars=None semantic should automatically choose whether to concatenate all data variables or only those that already have the concat dimension, based on whether the concat dimension is new or existing. Internal library code should not trigger these warnings.

constraints.grounded: Existing behavior must be preserved when use_new_combine_kwarg_defaults is False (the default) and no warnings are emitted — i.e., only when old and new defaults would produce identical output should the warning be suppressed. FutureWarning must only be emitted at the user call level (via emit_user_level_warning), not from internal callers. Internal callers such as groupby _combine_apply, Dataset.to_dataframe_array, plot helpers, and map_blocks must pass explicit keyword values so they do not trigger deprecation warnings. The CombineKwargDefault sentinel must not be directly usable by users as a keyword argument value. The concat compat default ('equals') must be kept distinct from the merge/combine compat default ('no_conflicts'). ValueError must be raised when both data_vars='minimal' and coords='minimal' are specified for a new-dimension concatenation.
constraints.conceptual: The deprecation must be non-breaking in the current version — old behavior is preserved by default and only warnings are added. Internal library operations must not surface deprecation warnings to users. The opt-in mechanism must be a single global toggle. The warning must only fire when there is a genuine behavioral difference, not unconditionally. Error messages under new defaults must provide guidance about the default change to help users migrate.

behavior: concat(), merge(), combine_nested(), combine_by_coords(), and open_mfdataset() use CombineKwargDefault sentinel objects as default values for data_vars, coords, compat, and join parameters instead of hardcoded string defaults.
When use_new_combine_kwarg_defaults is False (default), CombineKwargDefault resolves to old default values (data_vars='all', coords='different', compat='no_conflicts'/'equals', join='outer').
When use_new_combine_kwarg_defaults is True, CombineKwargDefault resolves to new default values (data_vars=None, coords='minimal', compat='override', join='exact').

A FutureWarning is emitted when data_vars or coords defaults would cause different variables to be concatenated under old vs new defaults (detected by comparing the concat_over set before and after processing).
A FutureWarning is emitted when compat default change from 'no_conflicts' to 'override' would affect merge results for overlapping variables that are not provably equal.
A FutureWarning is emitted when join default change from 'outer' to 'exact' would cause an AlignmentError due to unequal indexes that would otherwise be outer-joined.
When compat resolves to 'override' and coords/data_vars is 'different', a FutureWarning is emitted followed by a ValueError since 'different' is incompatible with 'override'.
data_vars=None resolves to 'all' when concatenating along a new dimension (dim not present in any input) and 'minimal' when concatenating along an existing dimension.
Specifying both data_vars='minimal' and coords='minimal' when concatenating over a new dimension raises ValueError.
AlignmentError and MergeError messages are augmented with migration guidance when the error occurs under new defaults via CombineKwargDefault.error_message().
set_options(use_new_combine_kwarg_defaults=True/False) controls which defaults are active; validated as boolean.

Internal callers (groupby combine, Dataset.to_stacked_array, plot data preparation, map_blocks, dataset_update_method, merge_data_and_coords) pass explicit keyword arguments to avoid triggering FutureWarning.
Dataset.merge() method signature updated to accept CombineKwargDefault for compat and join, propagating the deprecation cycle to the instance method.
acceptance_criteria: When calling xr.concat(datasets, dim) without explicit data_vars/coords/compat/join and old defaults would produce different output than new defaults, a FutureWarning is raised.
When calling xr.merge(datasets) without explicit compat/join and old defaults would produce different output than new defaults, a FutureWarning is raised.
When calling xr.combine_by_coords(datasets) without explicit keyword arguments and old defaults would produce different output, a FutureWarning is raised.
When calling xr.combine_nested(datasets, concat_dim) without explicit keyword arguments and old defaults would produce different output, a FutureWarning is raised.
When calling xr.open_mfdataset(paths) without explicit keyword arguments and old defaults would produce different output, a FutureWarning is raised.
When calling any combine function with all keyword arguments explicitly set, no FutureWarning is raised regardless of the use_new_combine_kwarg_defaults option.
When set_options(use_new_combine_kwarg_defaults=True) is active, concat/merge/combine functions use data_vars=None, coords='minimal', compat='override', join='exact' as defaults.

When set_options(use_new_combine_kwarg_defaults=False) is active (the default), concat/merge/combine functions use the old default values (data_vars='all', coords='different', compat='no_conflicts'/'equals', join='outer').
When data_vars=None is passed to concat and the concat dimension is new, all data variables are concatenated; when the dimension already exists, only minimal data variables are concatenated.
When data_vars='minimal' and coords='minimal' are both specified for concatenation over a new dimension, a ValueError is raised.
When an AlignmentError occurs under new defaults (join='exact'), the error message includes guidance about the default change and recommends setting join explicitly.
When a MergeError occurs under new defaults (compat='override'), the error message includes guidance about the default change.
Internal groupby, plot, parallel, and dataset operations do not emit FutureWarning about combine kwarg defaults.
set_options accepts use_new_combine_kwarg_defaults as a boolean and rejects non-boolean values.

task_10.title: Fix default engine detection to include h5netcdf as a fallback
task_10.description: The default netCDF engine selection logic in xarray did not consider h5netcdf as a candidate backend. When a user had only h5netcdf installed (without netCDF4 or scipy), calling to_netcdf(), open_dataset(), or open_dataarray() without explicitly specifying an engine raised a ValueError, despite h5netcdf being a fully supported backend. The fix adds h5netcdf to the engine fallback chain between netcdf4 and scipy, and switches the detection mechanism from try/except imports to importlib.util.find_spec for cleaner module availability checking.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that xarray automatically detects and selects the h5netcdf backend engine when it is the only netCDF-capable package installed. Previously, calling to_netcdf(), open_dataset(), or open_dataarray() without specifying an engine would raise a ValueError if only h5netcdf was available, because the default engine resolution logic only checked for netCDF4 and scipy.

expectation.grounded: _get_default_engine_netcdf() must return 'h5netcdf' when the netCDF4 module is not available but h5netcdf is installed. The function's return type must be Literal['netcdf4', 'h5netcdf', 'scipy']. The fallback priority order must be: netcdf4 first, then h5netcdf, then scipy. Module availability must be checked via importlib.util.find_spec rather than direct imports. When none of the three backends are available, a ValueError must be raised that names all three packages (netCDF4-python, h5netcdf, scipy). The open_dataset and open_dataarray docstrings must reflect h5netcdf as a supported backend for bytes, memoryview, and file-like inputs.
expectation.conceptual: When a user calls any netCDF read or write operation without explicitly specifying an engine, xarray should automatically detect and use whichever supported backend is installed. The detection should follow a defined priority order: netcdf4 is preferred, h5netcdf is the secondary fallback, and scipy is the tertiary fallback. If no supported backend is installed, the error message should clearly list all three supported options.

constraints.grounded: The fallback priority order netcdf4 > h5netcdf > scipy must be preserved. When netCDF4 is available, it must still be selected as the default engine (no regression). When both netCDF4 and h5netcdf are available, netcdf4 must be chosen. The ValueError raised when no backends are found must mention all three packages. The _get_default_engine_netcdf function signature and return type must include h5netcdf in its Literal union.
constraints.conceptual: The existing default engine preference for netcdf4 must not be altered. Users who already have netCDF4 or scipy installed must see no change in behavior. The fix must only expand coverage to recognize h5netcdf as a valid fallback, not change the priority of existing backends.

behavior: When only h5netcdf is installed, _get_default_engine_netcdf() returns 'h5netcdf' instead of raising a ValueError.
The engine fallback order is netcdf4 -> h5netcdf -> scipy, checked via importlib.util.find_spec.
When no netCDF backend is installed, a ValueError is raised whose message names netCDF4-python, h5netcdf, and scipy as the required packages.
to_netcdf() succeeds without an explicit engine argument when only h5netcdf is available.
open_dataset() and open_dataarray() succeed without an explicit engine argument when only h5netcdf is available.
When netCDF4 is available, it is still selected as the default engine regardless of h5netcdf availability.
acceptance_criteria: When only h5netcdf is installed (netCDF4 and scipy are absent), calling to_netcdf() without specifying an engine should succeed and use h5netcdf.
When only h5netcdf is installed, calling open_dataset() on a netCDF file without specifying an engine should succeed and use h5netcdf.
When netCDF4 is installed, the default engine should remain netcdf4 regardless of whether h5netcdf is also installed.
When both netCDF4 and h5netcdf are absent but scipy is installed, the default engine should remain scipy.
When none of netCDF4, h5netcdf, or scipy are installed, a ValueError should be raised that mentions all three packages as installation options.
Given h5netcdf is installed and netCDF4 is not, when _get_default_engine_netcdf() is called, it should return 'h5netcdf'.

task_11.title: Fix merge() to prevent mutating original input objects' attributes
task_11.description: Calling xarray.merge() or Dataset.merge() with certain join values (notably 'exact' and 'override') could silently mutate the .attrs of original input variables. This occurred because the merged variable was sometimes stored by reference without a shallow copy before attribute reassignment. The fix ensures a defensive shallow copy is always created before assigning merged attributes, making merge side-effect-free with respect to its inputs. Additionally, a FutureWarning is now emitted when merging overlapping variables under the default no_conflicts compatibility mode to alert users of potentially changing behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that xarray.merge() and Dataset.merge() do not mutate the attributes (.attrs) of original input Dataset or DataArray objects when any join mode is used. Previously, using join values such as 'exact' or 'override' could silently alter the original objects' attributes as a side effect of the merge operation. Additionally, ensure that users are warned via a FutureWarning when merging overlapping variables under the default no_conflicts compatibility mode, as results may differ in the future.

expectation.grounded: After calling xarray.merge() or Dataset.merge() with any join parameter value (including 'exact' and 'override'), the .attrs dictionaries of the original input variables must remain identical to their pre-merge state. The merge_collected function must produce a shallow copy of any variable before assigning merged attributes. The unique_variable function must return an equality indicator alongside the merged variable. When compat is the default CombineKwargDefault with value 'no_conflicts', there are multiple overlapping variables, and they are not equal, emit_user_level_warning must emit a FutureWarning.
expectation.conceptual: Merging datasets must be a side-effect-free operation with respect to all input objects. No input dataset's variable attributes should be modified as a consequence of a merge call, regardless of the join strategy. Users should receive a FutureWarning when merging overlapping variables under the default compatibility mode to signal upcoming behavioral changes.

constraints.grounded: The shallow copy before attribute assignment must only be created when necessary — specifically when either the variable already carries .attrs or the merged attrs dict is non-empty. The FutureWarning must only fire when compat is a CombineKwargDefault equal to 'no_conflicts', there are more than one variables, and the equality check returns False. Existing merge results (values, indexes, coordinates) must remain unchanged across all join modes. No MergeError behavior may be altered.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must not alter any merge output values or raise new errors. Performance overhead from defensive copying should be minimized by only copying when attribute assignment is actually needed. The FutureWarning should only appear in the specific scenario of overlapping variables under the default compatibility setting, not in explicitly user-specified modes.

behavior: When merge is called with join='exact' or join='override', the original input datasets' variable .attrs remain unmodified after the merge completes.
When merge is called with any join mode ('inner', 'outer', 'left', 'right', 'exact', 'override'), input variable attributes are never mutated as a side effect.
A shallow copy of the merged variable is created before assigning merged attributes, but only when either the variable or the merged attrs are non-empty.
The unique_variable function now returns an equality indicator alongside the merged variable, enabling downstream warning logic.
A FutureWarning is emitted when merging multiple overlapping variables under the default no_conflicts compatibility mode and the variables are not determined to be equal.
The FutureWarning is not emitted when compat is explicitly set by the user or when only a single variable is present.
acceptance_criteria: When merging two datasets with join='exact' where variables have attributes, the original datasets' .attrs dictionaries remain unchanged after the merge call.
When merging two datasets with join='override' where variables have attributes, the original datasets' .attrs dictionaries remain unchanged after the merge call.
When merging two datasets with join='outer' (or any other join mode), the original input objects are not mutated.
When merging datasets with overlapping, non-equal variables under the default no_conflicts compat mode, a FutureWarning is raised.
When merging datasets with overlapping variables that are equal, no FutureWarning is raised.
When merging datasets with an explicitly specified compat value (not the default), no FutureWarning is raised even for overlapping non-equal variables.
Merge output values, indexes, and coordinates remain identical to the pre-fix behavior across all join modes.

task_13.title: Clarify chunks=None lazy behavior and eager loading in open_* functions
task_13.description: The documentation for the chunks parameter in open_dataset(), open_dataarray(), open_datatree(), open_groups(), and open_zarr() previously stated that chunks=None simply 'skips using dask, which is generally faster for small arrays.' This was misleading because it omitted the crucial detail that while data appears lazy initially (via internal lazy indexing), it is eagerly loaded into memory as numpy arrays when accessed. Users working with large remote datasets (e.g., compressed Zarr stores on S3) experienced unexpected memory spikes when they assumed chunks=None kept data lazy throughout processing. The updated docstrings now explicitly state that chunks=None uses internal lazy indexing classes but that data is eagerly materialized into numpy arrays upon access, and that this mode is most efficient for smaller arrays or when large arrays are sliced before computation.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the documentation for the chunks parameter in open_dataset(), open_dataarray(), open_datatree(), open_groups(), and open_zarr() clearly communicates the memory loading semantics of chunks=None. Specifically, it must be made clear that: (1) chunks=None does not use dask, (2) data is initially represented via internal lazy indexing, but (3) data is eagerly loaded into memory as numpy arrays when accessed. The previous wording ('skips using dask, which is generally faster for small arrays') was insufficient and led users to believe data would remain lazy throughout their workflow, causing unexpected memory consumption with large datasets.

expectation.grounded: The docstrings for the chunks parameter in open_dataset(), open_dataarray(), open_datatree(), open_groups(), and open_zarr() must describe chunks=None as: skipping dask, using internal lazy indexing classes, but eagerly loading data into memory as numpy arrays when accessed. The documentation for open_dataset() should note efficiency for smaller arrays or when large arrays are sliced before computation. The documentation for open_dataarray(), open_datatree(), open_groups(), and open_zarr() should note efficiency for smaller arrays with a general caveat that results may vary.
expectation.conceptual: When a user reads the documentation for any of the open_* data-loading functions, the description of chunks=None must make the eager-on-access memory behavior explicit so that users can make informed decisions about whether to use dask chunking for large datasets. The documentation should guide users toward understanding that chunks=None is best suited for small arrays or large arrays that will be sliced before computation, and that for large datasets where lazy evaluation is needed throughout processing, a dask-backed chunking option should be used instead.

constraints.grounded: The chunks=None documentation must not imply that data remains lazy after access. The existing documentation for other chunks options (chunks='auto', chunks=-1, chunks={}) must remain unchanged. No runtime behavior of any open_* function is modified.
constraints.conceptual: The documentation update must not alter any function signatures, defaults, or runtime behavior. It must only improve the accuracy and clarity of existing parameter descriptions. The guidance must be consistent across all five open_* functions.

behavior: The chunks parameter docstring for open_dataset() describes chunks=None as skipping dask, using internal lazy indexing, and eagerly loading data into memory as numpy arrays when accessed, noting efficiency for smaller arrays or when large arrays are sliced before computation.

The chunks parameter docstring for open_dataarray() describes chunks=None as skipping dask, using internal lazy indexing, and eagerly loading data into memory as numpy arrays when accessed, noting efficiency for smaller arrays.

The chunks parameter docstring for open_datatree() describes chunks=None as skipping dask, using internal lazy indexing, and eagerly loading data into memory as numpy arrays when accessed, noting efficiency for smaller arrays.

The chunks parameter docstring for open_groups() describes chunks=None as skipping dask, using internal lazy indexing, and eagerly loading data into memory as numpy arrays when accessed, noting efficiency for smaller arrays.

The chunks parameter docstring for open_zarr() describes chunks=None as skipping dask, using internal lazy indexing, and eagerly loading data into memory as numpy arrays when accessed, noting efficiency for smaller arrays.
No runtime behavior changes occur in any of the five functions.
acceptance_criteria: When a user reads the docstring for the chunks parameter on open_dataset(), open_dataarray(), open_datatree(), open_groups(), or open_zarr(), the chunks=None entry clearly states that dask is not used.

When a user reads the chunks=None entry in any of the five open_* functions, it explicitly mentions that internal lazy indexing is used but data is eagerly loaded into memory as numpy arrays when accessed.
When a user reads the chunks=None entry in open_dataset(), it mentions efficiency for smaller arrays or when large arrays are sliced before computation.
When a user reads the chunks=None entry in open_dataarray(), open_datatree(), open_groups(), or open_zarr(), it mentions efficiency for smaller arrays with a note that results may vary.
When calling any of the five open_* functions with chunks=None, the runtime behavior is identical to the previous version (no functional regression).
The documentation for other chunks options (chunks='auto', chunks=-1, chunks={}) remains unchanged across all five functions.

task_12.title: Validate unlimited_dims in to_netcdf against actual dataset dimensions
task_12.description: When writing netCDF files via DataArray.to_netcdf(), Dataset.to_netcdf(), or DataTree.to_netcdf(), the unlimited_dims parameter (whether passed explicitly or inherited from dataset.encoding) was not validated against the actual dimensions of the object. After operations like swap_dims or rename_dims, stale dimension names could persist in encoding['unlimited_dims'], causing cryptic TypeError crashes deep in the h5py/h5netcdf stack when attempting to resize non-existent dimensions. The fix introduces upfront validation that raises a clear ValueError when unlimited_dims references dimensions not present in the dataset.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that unlimited_dims passed to xarray.DataArray.to_netcdf(), xarray.Dataset.to_netcdf(), or xarray.DataTree.to_netcdf() — whether supplied as an explicit keyword argument or inherited from dataset.encoding['unlimited_dims'] — only contains dimension names that are actually present in the object being written. When unlimited_dims contains dimension names not in the dataset (e.g., after swap_dims or rename_dims operations leave stale entries), a clear ValueError must be raised before any I/O is attempted, instead of allowing a cryptic TypeError to propagate from the underlying storage backend.

expectation.grounded: When to_netcdf() is called, a sanitization step must resolve unlimited_dims from either the explicit keyword argument or the fallback dataset.encoding['unlimited_dims']. The resolved value must be normalized (string and non-iterable inputs converted to a collection). The set of unlimited dimension names must be compared against dataset.dims. If any dimension in unlimited_dims is not found in dataset.dims, a ValueError must be raised before the backend store is opened. The error message must identify the undeclared dimension names and indicate whether they originated from the unlimited_dims keyword argument or from dataset.encoding. When all dimensions are valid, the sanitized unlimited_dims set must be passed through to the store layer. This validation applies uniformly across all netCDF engines (scipy, h5netcdf, netCDF4).
expectation.conceptual: When writing a dataset to netCDF, any unlimited dimensions declared — whether explicitly or via encoding — must be validated against the dataset's actual dimensions before I/O begins. Invalid dimension references must produce a clear, actionable ValueError rather than a low-level backend crash. The validation must work regardless of which storage engine is used.

constraints.grounded: Existing valid usage of unlimited_dims (where all specified dimensions exist in the dataset) must continue to work without behavioral changes. The unlimited_dims parameter must still accept a string, a sequence, or None. When unlimited_dims is None and dataset.encoding['unlimited_dims'] is also absent, no validation error should occur. The ValueError must be raised before the store is opened, ensuring no partial or corrupted files are created. The validation must cover both the explicit unlimited_dims keyword and the dataset.encoding fallback path.
constraints.conceptual: All previously working workflows where unlimited_dims correctly matches the dataset's dimensions must remain unaffected. The fix must not alter the semantics of valid unlimited_dims usage. Error reporting must happen early enough to prevent any side effects such as partial file writes. Both user-supplied and encoding-inherited unlimited dimension declarations must be validated.

behavior: When unlimited_dims is None, the value falls back to dataset.encoding.get('unlimited_dims', None); if that is also absent, no validation occurs and unlimited_dims remains None.
When unlimited_dims is a string or a non-iterable, it is normalized to a collection before validation.
When unlimited_dims contains dimension names not present in dataset.dims, a ValueError is raised identifying the undeclared dimensions and their source (keyword argument vs dataset.encoding).
When unlimited_dims contains only valid dimension names, the sanitized set is passed through to the backend store without error.
Validation occurs before the backend store is opened, preventing partial file writes or backend-specific crashes.
The error message distinguishes whether the invalid unlimited_dims originated from the explicit keyword argument or from dataset.encoding.
acceptance_criteria: When a Dataset has dimensions {'x', 'y'} and to_netcdf() is called with unlimited_dims=['x'], it should write successfully without error.
When a Dataset has dimensions {'x', 'y'} and to_netcdf() is called with unlimited_dims=['z'], it should raise ValueError before any file is written.

When a Dataset is loaded from a netCDF file with unlimited dimension 'test', then swap_dims is used to replace 'test' with 'something_else', calling to_netcdf() should raise ValueError because 'test' persists in encoding['unlimited_dims'] but is no longer a dataset dimension.
When unlimited_dims is passed as a single string (e.g., 'x') and that dimension exists, it should be accepted and normalized without error.
When unlimited_dims is None and dataset.encoding has no 'unlimited_dims' key, to_netcdf() should proceed without validation error.
When unlimited_dims contains an invalid dimension, the raised ValueError message should indicate which dimensions are invalid and whether they came from the keyword argument or from dataset.encoding.
When unlimited_dims contains invalid dimensions, no output file should be created or partially written.

task_14.title: Speed up Dataset.interp() for non-numeric scalar variables
task_14.description: Dataset.interp() exhibited linear scaling with indexer size when interpolating non-numeric (object, bytes, unicode) variables that had size 1 along the interpolated dimensions. This was caused by unconditionally collecting such variables for a costly reindex pass. The fix detects when a non-numeric variable is scalar-like (size 1) along all interpolated dimensions and uses broadcasting instead, achieving near-constant time regardless of indexer length.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Dataset.interp() does not degrade in performance proportionally to indexer size when the dataset contains non-numeric (object, bytes, or unicode dtype) variables whose size along the interpolated dimensions is 1. Previously, calling Dataset.interp() on such datasets with large indexers was orders of magnitude slower than necessary because all non-numeric variables were routed through a reindex path regardless of their shape.

expectation.grounded: When Dataset.interp() encounters a variable with dtype kind in ('O', 'b', 'U') and the variable has size 1 along every dimension present in the interpolation indexers, it should use broadcast_variables to expand the variable to the target shape instead of appending it to the reindex_vars collection. The resulting variable must be a deep copy of the broadcasted result. For non-numeric variables with size greater than 1 along any interpolated dimension, the existing reindex path must still be used.
expectation.conceptual: When interpolating a dataset that contains non-numeric variables (strings, objects, booleans) that are effectively scalar along the interpolated dimensions, the operation should complete in approximately constant time with respect to the number of interpolation points. The output values for those variables should be identical to what the reindex path would have produced — the variable's single value broadcast across the new coordinates.

constraints.grounded: Non-numeric variables with size greater than 1 along any interpolated dimension must continue to use the reindex path. The broadcast path must produce a deep copy so that mutations to the result do not affect the source variable. The dtype of non-numeric variables must be preserved through the broadcast path. Variables whose dimensions do not overlap with the interpolation indexers must remain unaffected. Dask-backed non-numeric scalar variables must also benefit from the optimization.
constraints.conceptual: The optimization must not alter the correctness of interpolation results for any variable type or shape. Existing behavior for multi-element non-numeric variables and all numeric variables must be fully preserved. The returned dataset must be independent of the source dataset's memory (no shared mutable state).

behavior: Dataset.interp() now checks whether each non-numeric variable has size 1 along all interpolated dimensions before deciding the code path.
Scalar-like non-numeric variables are squeezed and broadcast against the destination indexer coordinates, producing a deep copy of the expanded result.
Non-numeric variables with size greater than 1 along any interpolated dimension continue to be collected for the batch reindex pass, preserving prior behavior.
Performance for non-numeric scalar variables is now approximately constant regardless of the number of interpolation points, whereas it previously scaled linearly.
The optimization applies equally to eager (NumPy) and lazy (Dask) non-numeric arrays.
acceptance_criteria: When a Dataset contains a string variable of size 1 along the interpolated dimension and Dataset.interp() is called with indexers of varying lengths (e.g., 50, 100, 1000 points), the wall-clock time should remain approximately constant rather than scaling linearly.

When Dataset.interp() is called on a dataset with a string variable of size 1 along the interpolated dimension, the resulting variable should contain the original string value broadcast to match the new coordinate length.

When Dataset.interp() is called on a dataset with a non-numeric variable of size greater than 1 along an interpolated dimension, the variable should still be handled via reindex and produce correct results.
When Dataset.interp() produces a result with a broadcast non-numeric variable, mutating the result must not affect the original dataset (deep copy guarantee).
When a Dask-backed string variable of size 1 is present, Dataset.interp() should also avoid the slow reindex path and use broadcasting.
The dtype of non-numeric variables (object, bytes, unicode) must be preserved in the output after interpolation via the broadcast path.
